pairs.subject: generated-mesh-acceptance
pairs.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/ue-import-job-store.ts:159 The import job runs the Tier-1 critic only to plan collision and scale, then calls the importer whatever the verdict was. No branch checks for a 'fail', so a mesh the structural gate rejected (for example floaters or an empty mesh) still enters the UE project, and the ue-import status route does not even report the verdict.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/ue-import-job-store.ts:159 The scorecard itself (mesh-score.ts) is sound: findings come first, the score is 100-50·fails-15·warns, and density is only a warn. But the engine-entry edge ignores its fail verdict, and the job's comment at lines 114-116 says the critic is best-effort on purpose.

src/app/api/visual-gen/mesh-finish/remediate/route.ts:99 The route returns stable fail codes taken from typed findings, not parsed from the reason strings. Routing goes through the FINISH_RESOLVES / REROLL_RESOLVES lists in critique-stage.ts.

src/app/api/visual-gen/mesh-finish/remediate/route.ts:44 The remediate edge declares the stage explicitly and attaches assessStage's caveat to the result. The ue-import path is weaker: importStageFor (ue-import-job-store.ts:102) infers the stage from the file's directory instead of taking it from the caller. That is not the density proxy the technique forbids, but it is still an inference.

src/app/api/visual-gen/mesh-finish/route.ts:36 The route refuses cullInterior by name and states the adjacency corollary. The remediate route will not run a finish on a failure caused only by floaters, because decimation multiplies them. The face-share split itself is in component-split.ts, with the 0.5% share and 8-face floor, and truncated histograms resolve toward the harsher verdict.

src/app/api/visual-gen/ue-import/status/route.ts:62 Fields that were read back are an explicit null when nothing measured them, so absence is never read as a pass. mesh-finish/status also reports skipped and failed bakes rather than dropping them.

pairs.subject: generated-mesh-acceptance
pairs.evidence: scripts/visual-gen/pof_mesh_seethrough.py:103 By default the see-through sweep rotates every limb group ±75° on each axis instead of using the poses the character's actions actually reach. That is the blind sweep the technique names as a failure: frames are spent on unreachable poses whose folds drown the gap signal.

techniques.evidence: scripts/visual-gen/pof_mesh_seethrough.py:103 Several parts are right: six cameras (line 94), back faces shaded magenta on a transparent film, a closed or holed voxel-remesh control fixture, and enclosed background reported separately. The pose set, however, is not declared from the actions.

scripts/visual-gen/pof_mesh_split.py:179 Specks are classified by face share (default 0.005), not by count. Components dropped by the cap are counted separately from specks, and a coverage gate refuses to split a shattered mesh. pof_mesh_finish.py:197 also documents that the interior cull sees only welded interior.

scripts/visual-gen/pof_mesh_finish.py:487 An unmeasured UV stretch emits its own marker rather than a 0. A smaller lapse in the see-through script: lines 147-148 coerce a None backface_share to 0 when computing rest/posed max.
